title: Al-Ghazali Completes The Incoherence of the Philosophers
dek: In January 1095 at the Nizamiyya he finishes a refutation of twenty theses and brands three of them unbelief.
body: 11 Muharram 488, the day recorded in Istanbul manuscript Fatih 2921.

panels.label: Ghazali Argued
panels.text: Al-Ghazali argued that twenty theses of the falasifa fall short of demonstration, and that three are unbelief: an eternal world, a God who knows only universals, and souls that do not return to bodies.

panels.label: Averroes Argued
panels.text: Averroes argued, in The Incoherence of the Incoherence, that al-Ghazali had misjudged which of the philosophers' arguments count as demonstration.

panels.label: The Stakes
panels.text: Both camps claimed a warrant to settle what a Muslim must affirm. At stake was who draws the line of unbelief: the jurist at the Nizamiyya, or the philosophers' proofs.
